chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said:

Indeed, my mother had made a vow upon herself for Allah: if Allah were to return one of her children from something she feared for him, she would fast on the day he returns, as long as she lived. So she traveled with us to Mecca, and it became doubtful upon us; we did not know whether she should fast or break her fast. So I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about that, and informed him of what she had vowed upon herself. He said: 'She should not fast during the journey, for Allah has exempted her from His right regarding the fast, but she should fast what she has made upon herself [as the vow].'
He said: I asked, 'What do you think if she returns and neglects that?' He said: 'I fear that she might see in that which she vowed what she dislikes [i.e., a consequence or sign of displeasure].'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.حَقَّهُ: His right (referring to Allah's right of the fast)
key_terms.نَذْرًا: Vow (a voluntary commitment to perform an act of worship)

ai.seo_question: Does a traveler who made a vow to fast upon a specific event need to fast while traveling or only after returning?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Shia juristic distinction between the obligatory fast of Ramadan and a specific vow (nadh), ruling that the traveler's exemption applies to the former but not the latter. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while she is excused from fasting during the journey due to travel, she must still fulfill the vow upon her return, warning that neglecting it may lead to spiritual regret. This underscores the principle that personal vows retain their binding force even when general religious obligations are temporarily lifted.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara who said,

‘My mother had made it upon herself for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, a vow that if Allah<sup>azwj</sup> were to Return one of her children from something which she had feared upon, she would be Fasting that day in which he comes back, for as long as she remained. So she went out with us on a journey to Makkah. So it became doubtful upon us. We did not know whether she should be Fasting or breaking. So I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about that, and I informed him with what she had made it to be upon herself. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She should not be Fasting during the journey. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Exempted it from her His<sup>azwj</sup> Right, and she should be Fasting what she has made it to be upon herself’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view when she returns and neglects that?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> fear that she might see in that which she had vowed, what she dislikes’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has said the following:

“My mother had placed upon herself from Allah to fast a certain day if Allah returned one of her children safely from the danger of which she was afraid, and she would then fast the day her child came back. She did not stay; instead came out with us for Makkah and it became difficult for us because we did not know whether she was required to fast or not. I then asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about it and explained to him (the Imam) what she had done. He (the Imam) said, ’She is not required to fast on a journey. Allah has exempted her of His rights: why then must she fast because of what she has placed from Allah upon herself?’

I then asked him (the Imam), ‘What will happen if she did not do it at all?’ He (the Imam) said, ’If so, I fear for her to experience in the matter for which she had vowed to see what she may dislike.’”
